entities.summary:
Titus Aebutius Helva was a prominent Roman senator and general from the early Republic, serving as magister equitum under Aulus Postumius Albus at the Battle of Lake Regillus. He held the consulship in 499 BC and was the father of Lucius Aebutius Helva, consul in 463 BC.

As a key figure in the Roman Republic, Titus Aebutius Helva played a significant role in shaping the country's military and political landscape. His leadership during the Battle of Lake Regillus showcased his tactical prowess, and his subsequent consulship demonstrates his commitment to the welfare of Rome.

Titus Aebutius Helva's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his son Lucius Aebutius Helva would go on to follow in his footsteps, serving as consul in 463 BC and continuing the family's tradition of public service.

One striking aspect of Titus Aebutius Helva's career is the notable absence of any recorded conflicts or controversies surrounding his leadership, a testament to the stability and unity of the Roman Republic during this period.

In the pantheon of Roman generals, Titus Aebutius Helva stands as a notable figure, whose distinguished service and leadership qualities have been passed down through the centuries as a model for future generations of Roman leaders.
